summary.headline: Swastika Castal H1 FY27 standalone total income rose 24% YoY to Rs 21.25 crore, with EBITDA up 27% to Rs 3.34 crore and operating cash flow positive at Rs 1.04 crore.
summary.overview: Management said H1 FY27 was the first meaningful utilisation period for machinery commissioned in March 2026, after a stabilisation phase. Standalone total income was Rs 21.25 crore (up 24% YoY), EBITDA rose about 27% to Rs 3.34 crore and EBITDA margin improved to about 15%, with profit after tax also up. Cash flow turned positive at Rs 1.04 crore against an outflow of Rs 8.72 crore in H1 FY26. Management gave no quantified H2 revenue or utilisation guidance and said further capex would be announced only once finalised.

financial_highlights.change: improved YoY (exact prior figure not stated)
vs outflow of Rs 8.72 crore in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Total income FY26 (full year, as cited by analyst)

segments.name: Power transmission and electrical equipment (core)
segments.commentary: Management says this remains the core business, with the company supplying precision aluminium castings to OEMs such as Hitachi, Siemens, ABB, GE and Toshiba; analyst cited it as over 70% of the portfolio. Export share was about 41% of FY26 revenue, with customers in Europe, the US and Mexico.

segments.name: New customers (export and domestic)
segments.commentary: Two new customers added in the prior year are in early stages: the Trench customer has placed a first pilot-lot order and the Kuwak customer has approved its pilot lot and placed a first serial order. Full-scale revenue is expected in FY28; an Indian bushings customer is to receive its pilot lot in the current month.

segments.name: Railways, industrial and defence
segments.commentary: Early-stage diversification; management says one customer is in qualification and others are in discussion. Management frames these as long-term opportunities with no immediate significant revenue expected.

guidance_outlook: No quantified H2 FY27 revenue or volume guidance; management said it prefers not to give unsupported revenue commitments.

Margin expansion expected gradually via higher utilisation, material yield, machining and finishing value-addition, and procurement, but management flagged raw material, energy and pricing as offsetting factors.
Full-scale revenue from the Trench and Kuwak customers expected in FY28, per management.
Additional capex under evaluation; management will announce investment amount, capacity and commissioning schedule only once finalised. No timeline given.
Management aims to keep operating cash flow positive, with focus on inventory, receivables and working capital.
capex_capacity: Major expansion phase complete; machinery commissioned in March 2026 is operational, with a stabilisation period now behind it.
Current capacity utilisation not quantified; management said it would not quote figures until they are validated.
Small ongoing capex on machinery, furnaces, process improvements and pollution control; amounts not disclosed.
Radiography and some other non-destructive testing remains outsourced; in-house testing expansion depends on volume and customer requirement.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is available and growth is coming from existing customers, with new customers taking time to ramp.

Management cited an industry view that India transmission investment was about Rs 9.16 lakh crore over FY23-32 (the figure was spoken as '9.16 crore' and is likely a transcription error) and transmission additions in FY26 were about 37% above FY25.
Management is pursuing higher-value machined and finished components and in-house R&D and die design to improve realisations and margins.
No pricing or realisation figures were disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 24% income growth and how much came from volumes and new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited existing customer business, power T&D demand and the new machinery. Growth is mainly from existing customers; new customers are still ramping up, with one ramping now and another soon.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the EBITDA margin improvement and is further expansion possible?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA rose from Rs 2.62 crore to Rs 3.34 crore (about 27%), with margin near 15%. Drivers were fixed-cost absorption, lower rejections and better planning. Management sees gradual improvement but flagged raw material, energy and pricing as risks.

qa_highlights.question: How do you see H2 FY27 and what is the current capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: No H2 revenue commitment was given. Utilisation is rising gradually after stabilisation, with headroom available; no percentage was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow turn positive and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior-year cash was tied up in advance raw material buying and inventory. Management cites better inventory planning, receivables monitoring and production-dispatch coordination, and aims to keep cash flow positive, while still investing in small capex.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned capex by end FY27, with capacity and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier indication was only a possibility. Any further investment will be selective and demand-linked, and details will be shared once approved. No amount or timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Trench and Kuwak relationships and the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Both have passed audits and pilot lots; Kuwak has placed a first serial order and Trench a first pilot-lot order. Full-scale revenue expected in FY28. An Indian customer will get its pilot lot this month, and new OEM visits are planned for December.

risks_watch: Revenue concentration in power T&D and reliance on a few OEMs; new-customer volumes not yet material.
Lack of quantified utilisation and H2 guidance; watch for H2 revenue and capacity utilisation disclosures.
Working capital: operating cash flow was positive for H1 only after a large prior-year outflow; sustainability is untested.
Raw material and energy cost pass-through, and the margin trajectory against the stated 15% EBITDA margin.
Timing and size of further capex, which management has not yet defined.
Export exposure (about 41% of FY26 revenue) and dependence on foreign OEMs.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the operational story and the long-term power T&D outlook, but cautious and non-committal on numbers. Management declined to quantify utilisation, H2 revenue or capex amounts and often answered in general strategic terms.
key_quotes: Our focus is now shifting from building capacity to maximizing the potential of what that capacity that we have installed.
We are encouraged that profitability has grown faster than the revenue.
We prefer not to provide an unsupported revenue commitment.
